description: Base 14: next generalist gripper base, built on Base 12 (voice-98af07a6: compact gearbox, STS3215 smaller motor, wider finger spacing). Use the smaller STS3215 motor and attach the gripper to the reBot arm through the Mount part (Mount 1, the reBot wrist mount). Redesign the arm-side interface for the compact STS3215 base; keep it parameterized and printable without supports, with a clear center gripping area. Related: voice-3cd78d20 (Mount 1 / Base 10 arm mount), voice-a5d65841 (per-part picker).

results.identified_issue: Approach: Base 10's bracket bolted to the RS00 back face (4 M3 on 38). The STS3215 back face only has the idler horn and bus connectors; I had no reliable back-face hole data from the STEP params, and loading through the servo case is weaker anyway. So the base plate (already the structural member holding both pivot posts and the servo) got a tab (hull of leg_boss_r discs at (±wrist_screw_x, wrist_screw_z)), and the bracket leg (XZ plate, y in [base_y0-leg_t, base_y0]) clamps to the tab underside on the servo side. Leg top = wrist_screw_z+leg_boss_r must stay under the servo near end (sts_low_z, computed from the rotated case corners); asserted in gripper.scad, slider max -54.5. Gussets moved inboard (gusset_x) because at the leg edges they would hit the leg screw heads; gusset_len 10 keeps them under the servo. low_z for sts now uses the real servo/tab/pinion geometry (Base 12's formula wrongly used motor_d of the RS00). Code: gripper.scad uses leg_holes/leg_y1/tie_y so motor_sts 0 still builds Base 10's RS00 bracket (back_holes renamed back_holes_rs). Mount asserts no longer skip when sts. export_models/live_render/genus include bracket+tool_plate+hub and the arm with sts; aero_plate and the Aero Hand reference are dropped (the Aero Hand is its own family; Mount 1's aero plate stays owned by Base 10). check_geometry runs sts_checks plus mount_checks, with STS-specific bracket rows. Arm export needs cad/blender/.venv/bin/python (trimesh); run export twice on a fresh copy because previews render before arm() writes the arm STLs. Publisher: added Base 14 to the generations map and poses.js (pivot 31.35). Its heading carries Arm 1, Mount 1, which are already claimed by Base 10, so no duplicate catalog parts. Pre-existing unrelated failure: test_gripper_poses flags v306 with no poses.js entry. Not verified: printing, load and stiffness, the cable run to J6, and arm poses other than the exported one.
results.summary: Base 14 is Base 12 mounted on the reBot arm through Mount 1. The STS3215 base has a new wrist tab, and a new bracket clamps under it to hold Mount 1's tool plate. All 81 geometry checks pass.
results.detailed_description:
Base 14 builds on Base 12 and keeps its drive, fingers and STS3215 seat as they were. The STS3215's back face has no screw ring like the RS00's, so the base carries the arm load instead of the servo case. I added a wrist tab to the base's lower edge, 2 mm under the servo. A new wrist bracket's leg lies flat under that tab, beside the servo, held by 2 M3. Its foot sits across the J6 axis and takes Mount 1's tool plate on the usual 4 M3. The hub and tool plate are exactly Mount 1, so this gripper, Base 10 and the Aero Hand all swap on one hub.

Everything new is a params.json slider: wrist_screw_x and wrist_screw_z set the tab screws, plus wrist_pilot_d and gusset_x. Every part prints without supports (checked), and nothing sits between or in front of the fingers. The hub's arm face is 80 mm below the pivots. Nothing has been printed or load-tested: the gripper hangs on 2 M3 self-tapped into the 6 mm printed base.

Next: open Base 14 in the live preview with Arm 1 + Mount 1, and try the wrist sliders in Tune.

summary: Base 14 is a new gripper base using the smaller STS3215 motor, mounting to the reBot arm through Mount 1. The arm-side interface must be redesigned, parameterized, and printable without supports, with a clear center gripping area.
